Subject: Upgrade inquiry — Compact -> Throughput, feature bundling, proration

- How does feature bundling carry over on an upgrade? We have two legacy modules (prefix-cache and online-rerank) that are currently included; do they convert to add-ons or are they preserved in the new tier?

Hi Sasha — thanks for the note and the files. High level we can support both a near-term immediate upgrade (prorated) and a scheduled month-boundary upgrade. Practical options: 

1) Immediate upgrade (effective today)
   - Proration: standard daily proration applied to the higher-tier monthly fee; existing credits for unused reserved capacity will be applied against the first higher-tier invoice.
   - Feature handling: legacy modules (prefix-cache, online-rerank) can be preserved for 90 days while we migrate policies; if you opt to maintain them we’ll treat them as "legacy add-ons" (no additional charge for first 90 days). After 90 days they become billable add-ons under the Throughput SKU unless explicitly bundled in a commit.

2) Scheduled upgrade (effective at next billing boundary)
   - Full month credits: if you wait until 2026-11-01 the month will bill at Throughput rates and no proration applies — useful if you want a clean accounting cutover.
   - We can include feature-bundling within the annual commit so those modules are treated as included entitlements (requires signature on amendment).

Concession options we can offer (subject to deal size & term):
- 10% one-time onboarding credit for annualized 12-month commit (applied as credit on first invoice).
- If you commit to Dedicated capacity or a minimum monthly throughput floor we can explore a larger tiered discount (Ben can provide specifics).

I listed Ben and Priyom to chime in on commercial flexibility and rollout risk respectively. Next steps: tell me preferred effective date and whether procurement wants the amendment (DocuSign) with feature-bundling explicitly included.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett

Subject: Re: Upgrade inquiry — Compact -> Throughput, feature bundling, proration — rollout notes

Hi Sasha — technical context to help procurement/engineering decide: 

- Feature commutation: converting legacy modules to bundled entitlements is primarily a policy/ACL config. We can preserve the exact runtime behavior (no code changes) for 90 days while we flip entitlements; during that time prefix-cache and rerank remain in your tenant.
- Rollout suggestions: 1) schedule upgrade at a billing boundary; 2) enable features in canary (10% traffic) for 48–72 hours; 3) full cutover. This avoids cold-KV-cache issues that can spike latency.
- Cost/latency impact: retaining prefix-cache reduces token cost on repeated requests by ~12% compared to a fresh KV warmup; enabling higher throughput without quantization may increase per-token cost 6–9% on our hosted runtime. If you want to keep unit costs low, we recommend enabling 8-bit quantization profile for non-critical models (we can assist).
- Dependencies: if you request Dedicated capacity as part of the commit, lead time is 6–8 weeks for GPU pool allocation in us-west.

Happy to run a short playbook session with your infra team to map the canary steps.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.com
